top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping is a separable principle that lets very many neutral atoms be interrogated without a lattice light shift, and it has been reproduced across independent laboratories at the 1e-18 level. The two-name allocation fits the invention-plus-realization citation, and the work is mature. The reservations (metrology close to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, other lattice-clock groups left uncredited, no fundamental-physics result yet delivered) do not outweigh an award for a demonstrated invention, so I prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for P001 (no known connection to Katori or Ye); my TEM and microscopy-federation stake concerns B017, which is not on the slate, and Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, disclosed for transparency only
